messages:
matt: Ran a focused KV-cache quant experiment (INT8 vs FP8 w/ and w/o calibration) on rtx-dedicated pools. Quick writeup below — need a sanity check before we run canary.

matt: Setup: model gpt-large-like, seq_len=2048, batch=1/4, d_kv=512, baseline=fp16 KV.

matt: Raw KV sizes (per shard, measured with seq=2048, batch=1):
```
fp16: 16.0 MB
int8: 8.1 MB
fp8-no-calib: 8.7 MB
fp8-per-channel-calib: 9.4 MB
``` 

matt: Latency (single token decode, p50/p95 ms, batch=1):
```
fp16: 9.7 / 13.2
int8: 8.6 / 12.5
fp8-no-calib: 10.9 / 15.8  (sporadic 100-300ms spikes during dequant)
fp8-calib: 11.5 / 16.4
``` 

matt: Quality (next-token perplexity relative to fp16): int8 +0.9%, fp8-no-calib +4.1% (noticeable drift on >4k context), fp8-calib +1.4%.

priya: Nice. Do you have throughput numbers (tokens/sec) for batched workloads? Kernel selection matters there.

matt: Yes — batch=4, seq=512 steady-state tokens/sec (aggregate): fp16 1520, int8 1700 (+12%), fp8-calib 1480 (-2%). FP8-no-calib had higher variance and more retries.

lee: Any obvious root cause for fp8 spikes? kernel mismatch or dequant hotspots?

matt: Profiling shows two hotspots:
1) Dequant/quant roundtrips during KV read (FP8 path does per-chunk dequant for attention; expensive),
2) Extra cache thrashing when KV blocks are quantized with coarse shard boundaries. 

matt: Flamegraph snippet (abbreviated):
```
- attention_forward
  - kv_read_dequant
  - matmul_qk (int8_kernel)
  - attention_softmax
```

sasha: For kernel selection heuristics, propose: if seq_len>1024 or batch>2 prefer fp16 KV path; if seq_len<=1024 and batch>=2 prefer int8 path. Also fallback rules on spike rate >0.5%.

priya: Agree. Also we should try per-tensor vs per-channel calibration tradeoff — per-channel helps quality but adds ~10% dequant overhead.

matt: Experiment notes: per-channel calibration reduced perplexity back near int8 levels but added ~6-12% latency overhead depending on shard size. Overall memory wins still good.

lee: Can we push a canary with traffic shaping? I can run a small A/B on dedicated pool with 1% traffic.

sasha: SGTM. Let's also add a latency safety net: if p95 exceeds baseline p95 by >15% for 5m, auto-fallback to fp16 KV.

perf-bot: artifact uploaded: https://ci.redwood/inference/artifacts/1767102210/kv-quant-report.html :eyes:

matt: Next steps: (1) bake kernel-selection heuristic into runtime config (PR 4821), (2) run 1% canary w/ fallback rules, (3) run larger batched throughput tests for batch 8/16.

priya: I'll OWN calibration tuning and a compact eval harness focused on long-context drift.

lee: I'll schedule the canary window tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

sasha: Thx everyone :thumbsup:
